# Contacts — Overview, Contacts, Reports

**Status:** specified, not implemented
**Surface:** `/contact` in `apps/folk` and `apps/gita-life`
**Visual authority:** `_bmad-output/E-Assets/page-designs/contacts.figcraft`, generated by
`build_contacts_designs.py` — eight frames, light and dark, 1440×900 and 390×844.
**Behavioural authority:** this folder. `existing-state.md` carries the evidence,
`metrics-contract.md` defines every number, and the three page specifications are what an
implementer builds from.

---

## What this changes

`/contact` stops being a single form and becomes a **section**, in the place it already
occupies: the first pill in the desktop header, the first tab in the phone bottom bar.

| Route | Page | Tab label | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/contact` | **Overview** — five collection KPIs, each a link into a filtered grid | Overview | Admin, Preacher |
| `/contact/contacts` | **Contacts** — the grid that lives at `/manage?view=contacts` today | Contacts | Admin, Preacher |
| `/contact/reports` | **Reports** — funnel, monthly collection, collector leaderboard, data-quality list | Reports | Admin, Preacher |
| `/contact/new` | **New contact** — the form that lives at `/contact` today | — | every staff role |

`/manage` keeps Dashboard, Sessions, Attendance and Favorites. Its **Contacts tab is
removed**, and `?view=contacts` redirects to `/contact/contacts`, so every link already in
circulation still lands on the grid.

The job the section does: a coordinator opens the first pill and sees how many contacts were
collected, how many are usable, and where the holes are — then clicks any number to land on
the rows behind it. The design set's own cover states the same thing: *"the staff's contact
directory … the existing `/manage` grid as the third tab rather than the whole page."*

---

## Where this spec and the design set differ

The design set is adopted as drawn. Seven points were corrected, each because a field, a
convention or a decision makes the frame wrong rather than merely different. **All seven are
applied**: `contacts.figcraft` was regenerated from `build_contacts_designs.py` on 2026-11-01
and the frames now carry these. The table is kept as the record of what changed and why, so the
next reader does not re-open a question the build already closed.

| # | Design set | This spec | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A **sixth nav pill, "Contacts"**, beside the existing "Contact" | **No new pill.** The existing first pill hosts the section | Decided in review: one contact home, in the place the nav already gives it. The design file's extra nav item is removed from both the app bar and the phone bottom nav. |
| 2 | The Overview frame's page title reads **"Contacts"** | **"Overview"** | The title follows the tab the reader clicked, as on every Campaigns page and in `/manage`. A tab reading "Overview" over an `h1` reading "Contacts" is two names for one page. |
| 3 | The grid's hidden-field pill reads **"5 hidden fields"** | **"6 hidden fields"** | One derived, read-only `Collected` column is added, hidden by default (D4). The grid's *visible* eight columns are unchanged, which is what the frame draws. |
| 4 | The fourth tile reads **"Never contacted"**, `18`, `7%` | **"Never attended"**, counted on `totalAttendanceCount = 0` | No field can answer "never contacted" — `last_contacted_on` is parked empty by `20261010000000_contacts_date_columns_to_date.sql:125-131`. `existing-state.md` §12 has the evidence; open question 6 keeps the real metric alive. |
| 5 | One **"Unresolved"** row in the locations card, equal to the "No location" tile | **Two rows**: "No location" and "Unknown location" | A contact with no location and a contact whose location row was deleted are different facts — `spec-contacts-premium-grid` CAP-4, and `manage-contact-fields.ts:18-35` already ships two markers for them. Only the first is the tile's count. |
| 6 | The phone's Reports header shows `Last 90 days` as a **static subtitle** | The period is a **control**, full width under the title | A report whose window cannot be changed on the surface most readers use is a screenshot. |
| 7 | The phone draws a **pill strip** under the title | A **chevron and a full-screen menu panel** | One navigation per surface. The strip made three tabs compete with the section menu Campaigns already uses, and the panel is the app's own `campaign-menu.tsx`. |

Two things in the design were contested in drafting and are **kept**:

| Kept | Why |
|---|---|
| No period control on the Overview | Its windows are fixed and each caption names its own ("this month", "in 60 days"). A control that changed T1 "Total contacts" would change what "total" means. |
| Reports' `Export CSV` | It is in the frame and it is cheap: the same rows, the same window, the same functions (`ux-reports.md` §6). An earlier draft deferred it; that was wrong. |

One thing was decided after the first build and then reversed: **the phone's navigation**. The
spec first kept the design's pill strip on the argument that three labels fit 390px. They do,
but fitting is not the question — the section is entered from a chevron in the title on every
other surface, and a strip under that chevron is a second navigation competing with the first.
The phone now opens `campaign-menu.tsx`'s takeover panel, and the strip is gone.

Everything else — the five tiles and their order, the 860/480 card split, the four Overview
cards, the Reports cards, the toolbar, the table, the footer, the phone layouts and both
themes — is the design set's, unchanged.

---

## Decisions

**D1 — The Overview is numbers and links; the grid is the only detail surface.**
Chosen over a record drawer and over a per-contact route. The Overview therefore carries no
list of contacts and no expanded record. Every tile, every bar, every location row and every
collector row is a link into `/contact/contacts` with the filter that reproduces it. **A number
that cannot be reproduced as a row set may not be shown.**

**D2 — `/contact` is a bounded column, not a page-scrolling one.**
The one place the section deliberately differs from `campaigns/layout.tsx`. The grid must own
the page's only scroll container — `grid-scroll-surface.spec.ts` counts scrolling elements and
fails on a second one — and it can only do that if its ancestors hand it a bounded height
instead of letting the document grow. So the layout mirrors `apps/folk/app/manage/page.tsx`:
`h-[calc(100dvh_-_var(--mobile-app-nav-inset,0px))]`, `overflow-hidden`, `main` a
`min-h-0 flex-1` column. Overview, Reports and New contact each wrap their content in a
`min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto` region; Contacts continues the chain so the grid is the only
scroller.

**D3 — "Collected" is `initial_contact`, falling back to the record's creation day.**
`initial_contact` is the collection date and is what the design's month card already uses
("Contacts with a first-contact date, by month"). It is nullable, and **the grid's own
`+ Add record` create does not set it** (`lib/supabase/manage.ts:1094-1101`), so an
`initial_contact`-only basis would make every row created in the grid invisible to the KPIs.

The fallback is sound for historical rows as well, which is the part worth checking:
`scripts/migrate-airtable-data.mjs:677` maps `created_at` from `record.createdTime`, so a
migrated contact carries its **Airtable record creation time**, not the migration's run time.
The fallback therefore recovers a real date rather than inventing one on the day the data
moved.

Both are normalised to the `Asia/Kolkata` program day by the existing `calendarParts` helper
(`lib/supabase/manage.ts:228-252`). `metrics-contract.md` §1 states the derivation and the
`slice(0,10)` trap it avoids.

**D4 — One derived, read-only grid column, hidden by default.**
`Collected` (`collectedOn`) exists so a tile's link can reproduce the tile's count. It is
**hidden by default**, so the grid a reader lands on draws exactly the eight columns the
design's frame draws. It is **read-only**, so an inferred date can never be committed over a
stored one. `metrics-contract.md` §2 has the full argument and the cost.

**D5 — One chrome, shared with Campaigns, not copied from it.**
The design set's own premise is that "the two files read as one product". The code has to make
the same claim, so the chrome is extracted rather than redeclared:

| New file | Extracted from | Campaign keeps |
|---|---|---|
| `components/section-page-header.tsx` | `campaign/campaign-page-header.tsx` | `CampaignPageHeader` becomes a thin wrapper passing `CampaignMenu` |
| `components/section-menu.tsx` | `campaign/campaign-menu.tsx` | `CampaignMenu` keeps its props and its pending-count badge |
| `components/report-card.tsx` | `campaign/reports/report-card.tsx` | the five report cards import from the new path |
| `components/empty-state.tsx` | `campaign/campaign-empty-state.tsx` | `CampaignEmptyState` keeps its name and delegates |

Every campaign component keeps its public signature, so no campaign page changes and
`campaign-menu.spec.ts` guards the extraction.

**D6 — The grid moves; it is not rebuilt.**
`ManageContactsTable` is used as-is. Its columns, editors, commit and rollback path, row
lifecycle, keyboard model, selection semantics and URL contract are unchanged. What moves is
the container: from `ManagePortal`'s `TabsContent` into `/contact/contacts/page.tsx`. The
Admin scope switch moves with it — it was part of the `/manage` header rather than of the
grid, and it belongs to the section header on all three tabs because it narrows the server
read for every tab. The design puts it there too (`scope_switch` in every desktop frame).

**D7 — Tabs are shaped by role, and the section root has one meaning.**
Admin and Preacher see Overview · Contacts · Reports. **Volunteer and Assistant see no section
tabs** — they land on `/contact/new`, because they cannot read the grid: `contacts` RLS admits
an Assistant only through an assigned-preacher term
(`20261006010000_scoped_rls_policies.sql:173-181`) while the portal gate is
`requireRole(["Admin","Preacher"])`. A tab that 403s is worse than an absent tab. `/contact`
still means one thing for everyone: it redirects to `/contact/new` for the roles that cannot
read, so the login landing in `e2e/fixtures/roles.ts:47-48` keeps working with one hop.

**D8 — Both apps, mirrored.**
`staffContacts` is `true` for FOLK and Gita Life, and both apps render the same `ManagePortal`.
Moving the grid out of `/manage` in one app and not the other would fork the portal. So the
section is built in both, mirrored; the pages stay thin because every component is shared.
This is the one decision that changes Gita Life's staff experience, and it is recorded as such.

**D9 — Empty, loading and error states are specified, and the design set draws none.**
The frames are all populated. `ux-overview.md` §7, `ux-reports.md` §6 and `ux-contacts-grid.md`
§7 define each state, because `design-constraints.md`'s highest-leverage rule is that every
panel implements empty, loading and error, and all three are visually distinct. The design file
is a recording gap here, not a decision to ship without them.

---

## The New contact page

`/contact/new` is today's `/contact` page, moved. `ContactForm` is not touched: same fields,
same validation, same `POST /api/contact` body, same offline `202` and duplicate `409`
handling, same toast-and-reset after a save.

Four things change around it, nothing inside it:

- **No section header.** `/campaigns/new` renders only its form, and the form owns its head.
  `ContactForm`'s navy `New Contact` panel already is a head with a title and a subtitle
  (`contact-form.tsx:209-213`); stacking a 22px Poppins `h1` above it would give the page two
  titles at two sizes, neither of them the page name.
- **No sub-nav.** A reader mid-task does not need three tabs inviting them away. The form's
  save-and-reset flow is the loop, and it is designed to be repeated.
- **It scrolls.** The bounded layout means this page wraps `ContactForm` in
  `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto` and keeps the form's `max-w-2xl` centring.
- **It is the one page every role may open.** Volunteer and Assistant land here; Admin and
  Preacher reach it from the design's `Add record` toolbar button on the Contacts tab.

`/contact` therefore has one meaning per role, and the divergence is a redirect rather than two
pages at one URL:

```
reader (Admin, Preacher)  →  /contact  →  Overview
everyone else             →  /contact  →  redirect  →  /contact/new
```

---

## What must survive

The move must not be an opportunity to retune the grid.

- **One scroll container on the page** — `grid-scroll-surface.spec.ts:68` asserts it against
  the contacts surface and must pass in substance against `/contact/contacts`.
- **The URL contract** — `sort`, `q`, `f.<colId>`, `fa.<colId>`, `cols`, `hide`,
  `size.<colId>` (and `mode`) keep their names and meanings
  (`components/grid/grid-view-state.ts:8-16`). A saved grid link needs only its path swapped.
- **The grid's accessible name stays `Contacts`** — `e2e/fixtures/manage-grid.ts:84` locates
  the scroller by `getByRole("group", { name: "Contacts" })`.
- **`docs/manage-grid-pattern.md`'s rules** — DW-27's `ctx.text`, no `editable` column with a
  cell widget, the frozen identity run, hairline dividers, no row stripes.
- **`components/grid/` stays contacts-free and token-clean**:
  `grep -rn "dark:" components/grid/` → 0,
  `grep -rEn "#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}|rgb\(|white|black" components/grid/` → 0.
- **The phone view is still device-decided** — the list below `md`, the grid above. The
  section adds no view switch.

## Blast radius

Sourced in `existing-state.md`.

| Change | Files |
|---|---|
| Section shell | new `apps/*/app/contact/layout.tsx`, `components/contacts/contact-nav.ts`, `contact-page-header.tsx`, `contact-sub-nav.tsx` |
| New pages | `apps/*/app/contact/page.tsx` (replaced), `contact/reports/page.tsx`, `contact/contacts/page.tsx`, `contact/new/page.tsx` |
| The move | `components/manage/manage-portal.tsx` (tab removed), `components/manage/manage-types.ts` (`ManageView` loses `contacts`) |
| Extractions | `components/section-page-header.tsx`, `components/section-menu.tsx`, `components/report-card.tsx`, `components/empty-state.tsx` |
| Server | `lib/supabase/manage.ts` (`created_at` added to `CONTACT_COLUMNS`; `createdAt` and the derived `collectedOn` added to `ManageContact` and `ManageContactWriteResult`), new `lib/contacts/metrics.ts` |
| Reports export | new `apps/*/app/api/manage/contacts/export/route.ts` |
| Tests | `e2e/fixtures/manage-grid.ts:71-75`, `grid-scroll-surface.spec.ts:68`, `theme-switch.spec.ts:541`, `grid-toolbar.spec.ts:8,285,544`, `grid-column-drag-menu.spec.ts:39`, plus new `contact-overview.spec.ts`, `contact-reports.spec.ts`, `contact-export.spec.ts` |

`/api/manage/contacts*` keeps its name. The surface moved; renaming the endpoints would touch
every grid spec and every handler for a word.

---

## Non-goals

- **No contact detail route and no record drawer.** Decided in review: the grid is the detail
  surface. `§D1`.
- **No saved views, no Ask AI, no condition groups.** Unchanged from
  `spec-contacts-premium-grid`.
- **No new contact fields and no schema change.** `created_at` already exists on the table;
  it is only added to the select list, and `collectedOn` is derived, never stored.
- **No edit path outside the grid.** The grid is the only place a contact is written, exactly
  as `manage-contact-sheet.tsx:28-31` already states.
- **No change to the add-contact form's fields, validation or POST body.** It moves route, not
  shape.
- **No new chart dependency.** The month strip and the column chart are DOM, not Recharts
  (`ux-reports.md` §4.2).

| 1 | Should `createManageContact` write `initial_contact` on the grid's `+ Add record`? | The fallback makes those rows countable, but the collection *date* stays unknown. One line at `lib/supabase/manage.ts:1096`: `initial_contact: currentProgramDate()`. The design's "No first-contact date" row would then measure nothing for new rows and everything for history — which is the right shape. | 🔴 Open — recommended yes |
| 2 | Is the Assistant's access to the grid wanted? RLS already admits an Assistant to their preacher's contacts; only the portal gate excludes them. | Enabling it is a permission change, not a design change, so this spec does not make it. | 🔴 Open |
| 3 | Should `source` get a fixed vocabulary? `/api/contact` writes `"Pass distribution"` as a silent default, the grid's create writes nothing, and the grid's option list unions whatever the rows carry. | The design's "Where contacts came from" card and its "Everything else" row both depend on a vocabulary that does not exist. | 🔴 Open |
| 4 | How many months do the two collection cards show? The design drew five on the Overview and seven on Reports, both labelled as if fixed. | Settled while building: **six on the Overview, twelve on Reports**, each card stating its own window and pointing at the other. Twelve rows do not fit the Overview's 484px body above the sources card. | 🟢 Resolved — `ux-overview.md` §5.5, `metrics-contract.md` §6 |
| 5 | The Overview loads the whole contact table to compute its series. Acceptable at ~1,000 rows; at what count does it become an aggregate RPC? | The read is the same one the grid already does, so the cost is one payload. It is not free. | 🟡 In discussion — `metrics-contract.md` §6 |
| 6 | The design's fourth tile reads "Never contacted", and no field can answer it (`last_contacted_on` is parked empty). Should it be restored as **never called**, read from `dialer_call_logs`? | It is a real, actionable FOLK metric — "we have their number and have never rung them". It is dialer-only (`modules.dialer` is false for Gita Life), so the tile would be absent on one program, and it adds a fourth table to the read. The spec ships "Never attended" instead. | 🔴 Open — see `existing-state.md` §12 |
